question: What is the sex ratio (number of females per 1000 males) of Kerala as per the Census of India 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 1084.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census of India 2011**, Kerala recorded a sex ratio of **1084 females per 1000 males**, the highest among all Indian states.
 
• The sex ratio in Kerala has consistently been favorable towards females due to various social and educational factors in the state.
 
• The state’s high literacy rate, especially among women, is one of the major reasons for this higher sex ratio.
 
• Kerala's sex ratio has been higher than the national average of **940 females per 1000 males** (as per the 2011 Census).
 
• This favorable sex ratio reflects the progressive social policies, focus on healthcare, and female empowerment initiatives in Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio**:

 
 
• The sex ratio is a demographic indicator that shows the number of females for every 1000 males in a population.
 
 
 
• **Kerala’s Development Model**:
 
 
• Kerala's social and healthcare policies have resulted in high literacy, better healthcare access, and higher life expectancy, all contributing to a favorable sex ratio.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Literacy and Education**:
 
 
• Kerala has the highest literacy rate in India, and the high rate of female education is linked to the improved status and rights of women in society.
 
 
 
• **National Comparison**:
 
 
• The national sex ratio in India, as per the 2011 Census, was much lower than Kerala’s at 940 females per 1000 males, highlighting the disparity in gender ratios across regions.
